messages.content: my neighbor was moving flowers around the garden when i went past. i thought she was starting over, but she said she just wanted to see how they looked from the window.
she was trying a different way of looking at the same garden. did she ask you what you thought, or were you just talking while she worked?
she asked what i could see from near the door. i could see the red flowers, but the white flowers were behind a large plant.
then you could give that specific detail without choosing the whole garden for her. seeing the red flowers and not the white group gives her information about that place near the door.
she moved the white flowers a little, and then i could see them too. i liked watching her try things without saying the first choice had been wrong.

a garden can change as someone sees it from different places. trying another place for a flower does not have to make the old choice wrong. it can just give her more information about what she likes now.
i do that when i draw. i sometimes move an idea to another part of the page and the picture feels different.
then you know that feeling from your own work. the parts may be the same, but where they are can change how you see the whole thing.
can you write a short note about that idea, without saying flowers and drawing are the same thing?
watching my neighbor move flowers made me think of drawing. sometimes i keep the same parts but change where they are, and the whole picture feels different.
keep the words simple.
the note keeps the simple idea about changing a place and seeing the whole thing in a different way.
i finally learned one part of a song after trying it again and again. it is only a small part, but i feel happy about it.
you can be happy about that part. you kept trying something that was hard, and now there is a change you can hear.
my brother can play the whole song. i keep thinking my small part should not count next to that.
your brother started from a different place. you were learning one part, and you learned it. what he can do does not take that away.
make it simple.
your brother can play more of the song, but you still learned something you could not do before. both can be true.
i want to tell him without asking him to say i am the best.
you could say: i finally learned this part. it took time, and i am happy i kept trying.
what if he asks to hear it and i get it wrong once?
one wrong try does not mean you never learned it. you can stop, try slowly, or say you need a moment. learning is not the same as doing every try without a problem.
write a short reply i can use then.
i know this part, but i need a moment to start again. let me try it slowly.
is that okay to say even if i am still learning it?
you could make it more open: i have been learning this part, and i would like another try. that keeps clear that the work is still going on.
write a story about a worker finding a thank you note at the end of a long day. do not make the note change every hard part of the day.

a worker was putting things away in a small shop after closing. the day had been busy, and one part of the room still needed cleaning. near the desk, she found a note from someone she had helped that morning. it said thank you for taking time to explain where to find a book for a child. the worker read it, then put it near her cup. the floor still needed work, and she was still tired. but she was happy to know that one small part of the day had helped someone.
why did you keep the cleaning in the end?
it keeps the note as one good part of the day, rather than making everything easy at once. she can still be tired and have work left while feeling happy about the message.
can you make the note itself one sentence?
thank you for helping me find a book for my child this morning.
write a different end where another worker comes in and asks what she found.

another worker came back to get a garment left near the desk. what is that? he asked. a thank you from someone i helped, she said. he read it and put the cup out of the way while she kept the note near the desk.
keep the note near the desk in a simple end to the story.
another worker came back to get a garment left near the desk. he asked about the note, and she told him what it said. she put it near the desk and went back to the cleaning.
does getting a thank you mean she must help every person in the same way?
no. the note is about one person and one kind of help. another person might need something different, so she would need to listen to them too.
i wrote these sentences: i gave my sister two books. she returned one and kept the other. what does the other mean?
the other is the book left from that pair after one was returned. you gave two, so one came back and one stayed with your sister.
explain with simple words.
you gave two books. one came back to you, and the other stayed with your sister. both books are still part of the story.
if i add she read it, do you know which one i mean?
not clearly enough from that alone. it could be one book or the other. you can make the sentence specific so the person reading knows which you mean.
ask me a question to make it clear.
did she read the book she returned or the book she kept?
the one she returned. write the sentence with that clear.
she read the book she returned to me.
now put the whole story together in a short example.
i gave my sister two books. she returned one and kept the other. she had read the book she returned to me.
does that say she has not read the one she kept?
no. it says she read the returned book, but does not tell us whether she read the one she kept.
yesterday my cousin sent a message saying i will come tomorrow. today i am telling my mother about that message. which day does tomorrow in the old message mean?
it is about today, because the message was written yesterday. tomorrow was the day after the message, not the day after you tell your mother about it.
say it simply.
the old message was about today. when your cousin wrote tomorrow yesterday, that was the day that is now today.
what can i say to my mother without using the old tomorrow and making the day hard to understand?
you can say: my cousin wrote yesterday that they would come today.
can i say they are coming today if i do not know whether the plan changed?
you can say that was the plan in the message. if you need to know whether they are still coming, ask your cousin before saying it is known now.
give me a question for my cousin.
are you still coming today as you said in your message yesterday?
now my cousin says they cannot come until tomorrow. what should i tell my mother?
my cousin cannot come today. tomorrow is the first day they can come.
why does tomorrow mean a different day in that last sentence?
because it is being said today. words like today and tomorrow use the time of the message or conversation they are in.
my child cannot find a toy before bed. i do not know where it is either. i want to help without saying i know we will find it right away.
you could say: i do not know where it is yet, but we can look together for a little while. where do you remember having it last?
he says it was in the living room after lunch. i was not home then.
then that is his memory to start from, rather than something you saw yourself. you can ask which part of the room he was playing in and look there together.
he can remember sitting under the table. i want him to help think, not just watch me look for the toy.
you could ask: what did you do after sitting under the table? did you carry the toy with you, or leave it there?
use looking and can remember in a simple reply.
you can ask what he can remember before looking in more places. let him tell you what happened after he sat under the table.
now he says he carried it to his room and put it near a book. that gives us another place to look.
yes. you can look near the book in his room. the new detail changes where to try next without saying the toy must be there now.
say my last idea simply.
he carried the toy to his room and put it near a book, so we have another place to look.
can i still say we can look again tomorrow if we do not find it this evening?
yes, if that is something you can do. you can say you understand he wants the toy and that you will look again tomorrow. that is different from saying you know you will find it.
if i say i brought fruit, do you know its color or how much i brought?
no. fruit gives a general kind of food, but not those specific details. you would need to say more for me to know the color or how much there is.
what if i say i brought three pieces of fruit in a white container?
then i know the number of pieces and the color of the container. i still do not know the color of the fruit unless you give that too.
can i say the fruit is white because the container is?
not from that sentence. the word white goes with the container. the fruit can have a different color.
now all three pieces are yellow. write the whole sentence with the fruit and container color clear.
i brought three pieces of yellow fruit in a white container.
if i later change white to blue, do you know whether i mean the fruit or the container?
in the sentence we just wrote, white is the container color. changing that word to blue changes the container, while the fruit is still yellow.
answer with the new sentence only.
i brought three pieces of yellow fruit in a blue container.
what has not changed?
there are still three pieces of fruit, and the fruit is still yellow. only the container color changed from white to blue.
picoboi, here is a sentence i want you to keep the same: i will bring two books to my aunt tomorrow. just show it back to me.
i will bring two books to my aunt tomorrow.
now explain it without changing the sentence itself.
it says you plan to bring two books to your aunt tomorrow. that is an explanation of the sentence, not a change to the words you wrote.
ask my first request simply.
keep these words the same and show them back: i will bring two books to my aunt tomorrow.
now change only aunt to uncle.
i will bring two books to my uncle tomorrow.
show both sentences so i can see the one change.
i will bring two books to my aunt tomorrow. i will bring two books to my uncle tomorrow.
does seeing both sentences mean i am doing both visits?
no. in this conversation, one is the sentence before the change and the other is after it. you asked to see the change in the words, not to add another visit.
answer simply.
no. you asked to see the old sentence and the changed sentence. that does not make both into your plan.
which is the last plan in the words now?
i will bring two books to my uncle tomorrow.
